blocks.content: National Income is the MOST IMPORTANT and MOST SCORING chapter of  Economics. Questions from this chapter are direct, formula-based and concept-based.
PART A: CONCEPT OF NATIONAL INCOME

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The key aggregates of national income consist of GDP, GNP, NDP, and NNP.
National income metrics are evaluated at two distinct levels: Market Price (MP) and Factor Cost (FC).
Economic output is measured using Real GDP (adjusted for inflation) and Nominal GDP (at current prices).
Three primary methods are used to compute national income: Product (Value Added) Method, Income Method, and Expenditure Method.
Per Capita Income provides a measure of average income earned per person in a given population.

blocks.content: 1. Meaning of National Income

National Income refers to the total monetary value of all FINAL goods and services produced by the normal residents of a country during one financial year. It represents the income earned by factors of production such as land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.
National Income is used to measure the economic performance of a country, compare growth over time and frame economic policies.
PART B: BASIC NATIONAL INCOME AGGREGATES (WITH FORMULAS)
2. Gross Domestic Product (GDP)
GDP is the total monetary value of all FINAL goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during one year.

Formula:

GDP = Value of output produced within domestic territory



Key Points:

• Includes only final goods

• Includes production by foreigners within India

• Excludes income earned by Indians abroad
3. Gross National Product (GNP)
GNP measures the total income earned by the normal residents of a country.

Formula:

GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)



NFIA = Income earned by Indians abroad – Income earned by foreigners in India
4. Net Domestic Product (NDP)
NDP is obtained by deducting depreciation from GDP. Depreciation refers to wear and tear of capital goods.

Formula:

NDP = GDP – Depreciation
5. Net National Product (NNP)
NNP shows the actual income earned by the nation after allowing for depreciation.

Formula:

NNP = GNP – Depreciation
PART C: MARKET PRICE AND FACTOR COST (FORMULA BASED)
6. Market Price
Market Price is the price paid by consumers. It includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies.
7. Factor Cost
Factor Cost is the cost of production incurred by producers.

Formula:

Factor Cost = Market Price – Indirect Taxes + Subsidies
PART D: REAL GDP, NOMINAL GDP & GDP DEFLATOR
8. Nominal GDP
Nominal GDP is GDP measured at current prices. It is affected by inflation.
9. Real GDP
Real GDP is GDP measured at constant prices. It shows true economic growth.
10. GDP Deflator

rows: Less reliable for comparing real growth
Highly reliable indicator of true production growth

blocks.content: GDP Deflator is used to remove the effect of inflation.

Formula:

GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100
PART E: PER CAPITA INCOME (FORMULA)
11. Meaning of Per Capita Income
Per Capita Income is the average income of people in a country.

Formula:

Per Capita Income = National Income / Total Population
PART F: METHODS OF MEASURING NATIONAL INCOME (FORMULAS)
12. Product (Value Added) Method
National Income is calculated by summing value added at each stage of production.
13. Income Method
National Income is calculated by summing factor incomes.

Formula:

National Income = Wages + Rent + Interest + Profit
14. Expenditure Method

items: Formulas converting Gross to Net (Depreciation) and Market Price to Factor Cost (Net Indirect Taxes) are heavily tested in competitive exams.
Be prepared for direct numerical problems on calculating the GDP Deflator using Nominal GDP and Real GDP.
Questions frequently test the identification and components of the Product, Income, and Expenditure methods of measuring national income.

blocks.content: National Income is calculated by summing total expenditure.

Formula:

GDP = C + I + G + (X – M)
PART G: IMPORTANCE & LIMITATIONS
15. Importance of National Income
It helps in economic planning, policy making, comparison of growth and measurement of living standards.
16. Limitations of National Income
It ignores non-monetary activities, income inequality and environmental degradation.
ULTRA FINAL REVISION FORMULAS

• GDP = Value of final goods

• GNP = GDP + NFIA

• NDP = GDP – Depreciation

• NNP = GNP – Depreciation

• Factor Cost = Market Price – Indirect Tax + Subsidy

• GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) × 100

• Per Capita Income = NI / Population

• GDP (Expenditure) = C + I + G + (X – M)
